title: Delegated quota slices and escrowed shared credits for multi-team orgs
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Problem statement: Large organizations running multiple product teams want predictable per-team quotas while preserving economics of a single corporate plan. Today customers either get coarse-grained per-customer quotas or ad-hoc per-route rate limits. We need a first-class feature that lets org admins carve their purchased entitlement into 'delegated slices' assigned to teams or projects and optionally attach an escrowed shared credits pool that teams can draw from under configurable priority rules. This solves several needs: 1) clear per-team spend visibility for chargeback, 2) controlled overage behavior that avoids surprise invoices for teams, and 3) operational tools to reassign or reclaim quotas mid-cycle with correct prorations and audit trails.
background: Target customers: mid-market and enterprise platform teams that manage multiple product groups with separate budgets. Related work includes cross-tenant pooling (PM-24107), transferable entitlements (PM-36789), and invoice visibility improvements (PM-58823). This ticket defines the PM-level requirements and acceptance criteria; engineering will produce detailed API/DB schema designs in ENG-7421.
goals: Allow org admins to create fixed or percentage-based delegated slices from a purchased entitlement (tokens, monthly compute credits, and concurrency)
Provide an optional escrowed shared credits pool that multiple slices can draw from according to priority/decay rules
Ensure billing accurately attributes usage to the consuming slice and to the shared pool with line-item clarity on invoices and billing UI
Support mid-cycle slice adjustments with deterministic prorations and ledger events that can be audited
out_of_scope: Per-caller or per-route dynamic reweighting algorithms
Support for on-prem private deployments billing connector (handled in later phase)
requirements: Admin UX: 'Create slice' workflow in Console where admin selects parent entitlement, slice type (fixed units | percentage of parent), assigned team identifier, soft-limit and hard-limit values, and optional eligibility flags for shared pool draws.
API: POST/GET/PUT/DELETE endpoints under /v1/entitlements/slices with full audit metadata (actor, timestamp, reason).

Escrow pool: Ability to create one or more named escrow pools attached to a parent plan with config fields: total_amount, priority order, per-draw cap, time-decay schedule (optional), and emergency-shield boolean.

Enforcement: Runtime quota enforcement must deduct from slice bucket first; if exhausted attempt to draw from pools according to priority and per-draw caps; if no credit available apply configured fallback (soft-throttle, per-team rate-limit, or immediate rejection).

Billing: Usage attribution must produce three ledger categories: slice_usage, pool_usage, and overflow_charges. Invoices must contain per-team subtotals plus pooled consumption. Mid-cycle slice changes must produce ledger events for proration (credits moved, refunds, or additional charges) and these must be visible in invoice line items and audit logs.
Observability: Per-slice metrics in Console (tokens consumed, pool draws, average latency under pooled draws, count of fallback events). Traces/alerts when pool depletes below configured thresholds.
Security/compliance: All slice create/modify/delete actions must be captured in audit logs with user identity and IP; KMS metadata must be preserved for billing export payloads.
API contract: SDKs (Python/Node) should expose helpers for creating slices and querying remaining quotas; behavior must match Console exactly.
Acceptance tests: Synthetic workload harness that simulates concurrent multi-team bursts to validate atomicity of pool draws and no double-counting.
acceptance_criteria: AC-1: Admin can create a delegated slice (fixed units) and assign it to a team. Slice shows allocated units and remaining units in Console and via API within 30s of creation.

AC-2: When a team consumes tokens, system charges slice_usage until depleted, then draws from escrow pool according to priority rules. Pool draw events are recorded in ledger and visible in per-team usage view.

AC-3: If pool is empty and fallback is configured as soft-throttle, requests beyond slice should be delayed but not immediately rejected; metrics must reflect fallback events and Console must surface the reason.

AC-4: Mid-cycle reclamation of a slice (admin reduces allocation) creates a proration ledger event: remaining unused units returned to parent plan or escrow pool as configured, with corresponding refund/credit in billing preview.

AC-5: Invoice generation includes per-team line items: slice charges, pooled charges (allocated to teams or as shared line with breakdown), and any overflow charges. Finance team can reconcile subtotal totals to ledger events within 24 hours of invoice run.
AC-6: Audit logs contain entries for slice creation, modification, deletion, pool draws, and proration events. Each entry includes actor, timestamp, reason, and before/after balances.
AC-7: SDK APIs return consistent quota remaining values under concurrent requests (no negative remaining, eventual consistency within backend windows documented in API).

AC-8: End-to-end test harness demonstrates no usage double-counting in high concurrency scenario (100s of concurrent draws) and confirms latency SLO not degraded more than 5% for pooled draws versus direct slice draws.
AC-9: Feature flag gating exists so enterprise customers can opt-in; no behavior changes for customers who do not enable delegated slices.
AC-10: Security review sign-off recorded (if required) and audit export integrates with finance S3/KMS export pipeline for invoice reconciliation.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (beta): Expose API and Console create/read for fixed-unit slices and a single escrow pool; opt-in for invited enterprise customers; duration 4 weeks.
Phase 2: Add percentage-based slices, multiple pools, and proration ledger events; broaden to self-serve for all enterprise orgs.
Phase 3: UX polish, SDK helpers, and performance optimization; GA and documentation updates (billing docs and admin runbook).
metrics: Adoption: number of orgs creating at least one delegated slice within first 30 days
Operational: pool draw rate, pool depletion events per org per month, number of proration events per billing cycle
Billing correctness: discrepancy between ledger-sum and invoice line-items must be < $0.01 per invoice in 99.9% of cases
Performance: median latency for token consumption path under pooled draws vs baseline (SLO: <5% regression)
test_cases: TC-01: Create slice with fixed 100k tokens, simulate 90k consumption from team A: expect slice_usage=90k, remaining=10k.
TC-02: Simulate concurrent burst where team consumes 5x slice concurrently pushing over slice: confirm atomic pool draws, no negative balances, ledger entries per draw.
TC-03: Configure pool with per-draw cap=10k and priority order; simulate team attempting 50k draw: expect repeated capped draws until either satisfied or pool exhausted; verify per-draw caps honored.
TC-04: Reduce slice allocation mid-cycle and verify proration ledger event and billing preview reflects credit refunded to parent subscription or to specified pool.
TC-05: Generate invoice end-of-cycle and perform reconciliation script to compare invoice lines to ledger events; differences must be zero after rounding rules.
TC-06: Opt-out customers: ensure no change in billing or enforcement for orgs without delegated slices enabled.
TC-07: Security: verify audit log contains actor and IP for slice deletion and pool modification actions and that export to finance S3 contains required KMS metadata.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Incorrect proration could cause invoice disputes. Mitigation: implement ledger-first model with double-entry records and run reconciliation tests on staging data before GA.
Risk: High contention on pool draws may cause latency spikes. Mitigation: use atomic counters + local caching in serving runtime and backpressure thresholds; monitor and throttle non-critical flows.
Risk: Complexity in UI leads to admin errors. Mitigation: provide sensible defaults, templates, and a guided wizard with warnings for destructive changes.
Risk: Finance cannot reconcile pooled charges. Mitigation: add detailed per-usage export with mapping from ledger_event_id -> invoice_line_id and sample reconciliation script.
next_steps: Review with Finance and Legal for invoicing and proration language (target review meeting 2026-03-18).
Kick off engineering discovery (ENG-7421) to validate data model, API contract, and atomic draw semantics.
Design: produce Console flows and help text; prepare admin runbook and sample use-cases.
Support: prepare KB draft and incident playbook for pool depletion events.
notes: This approach intentionally separates enforcement semantics (runtime) from billing semantics (ledger). Runtime must emit idempotent draw events that billing system consumes to produce ledger entries.
We should consider a later extension to allow automated emergency top-ups from corporate card with explicit guardrails and approvals.
Track potential overlap with PM-24107 (cross-tenant pooling); decide ownership of feature set during discovery.
